editorial:
Imagine you are invited to a fancy party in the 1930s at a big house in the middle of nowhere. You have got high-society guests who act like they love each other, but really, they are all fighting and keeping secrets. The vibe starts off feeling like a posh dinner party, but it quickly turns into a total nightmare. Once a door to Hell opens up, the polite talking stops and the blood starts flowing. It is a wild mix of dark jokes and scary moments that keeps you guessing about who will survive the night.

You will really enjoy how the movie balances the laughs with the gross-out gore. The acting is great, especially since the characters are so over-the-top and mean to each other. While the plot gets a bit messy toward the end, the energy never drops. If you like movies that do not take themselves too seriously, you should definitely give this a try. You can rent it on Apple TV for a quick movie night, or if you are a collector, adding the 4K Blu-ray to your physical collection is the way to go for the best picture quality.
endingExplained: The movie ends in total chaos as the demon takes over. After all the fighting and betrayal among the guests, the gateway to Hell fully opens. Most of the characters meet a bloody end as the demonic forces win. The twist is that the social games they played earlier didn't matter because the evil was too strong. It wraps up with a dark realization that no one was truly innocent, leaving the house a scene of complete destruction.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves horror comedies with lots of blood and mean characters.
